subject: snail
pitch: A garden snail on an adventure. A glossy spiral shell striped in caramel, chocolate and cream, a soft grey-green body with a pebbly texture and a slimy shine, two long eye stalks with little black eyes and two short feelers below. A tiny ladybird hitches a ride on top of the shell.
reasoning:
I'll need to write this module without being able to test it, so I should stick to conservative, well-known API calls like createBuilder, joint, chain, sweep, part, and stick, while being mindful that I'm unsure about the exact joint signature for specifying a parent relationship.

Given the uncertainty around chain and sweep options, I'll play it safe by building the snail's body from basic parts (scaled spheres/capsules) attached to bones rather than risking an unfamiliar sweep API. I'm planning the skeleton layout now: a root body joint, head and tail joints, with the snail facing +Z, a compact body length, and a shell sized proportionally.

Working out joint positions for the foot, head, tail, and tentacle/eye stalks, then shaping the foot as a flattened capsule and the eye stalks as tilted cylinders built manually since the rod helper's signature is unclear.

I'll write a tube helper to orient cylinders between two points, baking rotation into geometry directly rather than relying on the bone transform. For the shell, I'm planning a logarithmic spiral of spheres tilted sideways on the snail's back, colored in alternating caramel, chocolate, and cream stripes.

Simplifying to a growing-radius spiral of overlapping spheres along the shell's whorl, with per-sphere coloring that cycles to create banding—though I'm weighing whether true lengthwise stripes along the spiral would look more realistic than cross-whorl banding.

For each step, I'll place a cluster of spheres across the tube's cross-section—one outward, two upper/lower-axis—cycling colors through caramel, chocolate, and cream, plus a central filler sphere, aiming for roughly 40 steps times 6 spheres kept low-poly for performance.

Now I'm working out the spiral geometry itself: path radius growing exponentially along the shell axis, tube thickness scaled relative to that radius, and adjusting the starting radius so the shell stays proportional to the snail's body rather than overwhelming it, with a slight conical offset along the axis for a planispiral look.

Working out the helical coordinates instead with axis Y so the apex points up, then tilting the whole shell backward with a rotation about X so the apex leans back and the largest whorl sits low at the front.

I'm tuning the shell's exact placement and growth constants: center position around y=0.036, growth rate k=0.16 giving a final whorl radius near 0.019 and tube radius about half that, while checking the lowest point after tilt stays just above the ground.

Working through the overlap math, I find the tilted shell's lowest point sits around y=0.01, nicely overlapping the body's top at 0.013, so the proportions feel right even if the shell reads a bit oversized and cute. I'll skip a cream lip detail for now and move to adding an apex sphere, then start thinking about placing a ladybird on top of the shell.

For the ladybird placement, I'm computing which whorl sample sits highest in world space (around θ=0.55 of θmax near the apex), then offsetting outward from that center by the tube radius plus a bit extra to sit it on the surface like a little red dome sphere.

Now for the snail body I'm layering details: a grey-green base with darker shading on top, scattered small bumps for a pebbly texture, and tiny pale highlight spheres for subtle shine. I'm adding a raised head sphere near the front, a body hump beneath the shell, and starting work on a tapered tail.

Feelers point down and forward with a small knob tip, and I'm adding a mouth with upper lip and lower jaw as flattened spheres at the front bottom of the head. I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy now—body as root, with tail, neck, head, jaw, eye stalks, feelers, shell, and ladybird all parented appropriately with their positions.

I'm sketching helper functions for adding parts: one that attaches geometry with color and bone binding at an explicit position, and another specifically for placing spheres by radius, position, color, and bone, baking any scaling directly into the geometry rather than relying on an uncertain scale option.

For tubes, I'm building cylinder geometry oriented between two points using a quaternion rotation and positioning it at the midpoint. For the ladybird shell, I'm planning a flattened hemispherical dome, a small black head sphere up front, several black spot spheres distributed around the dome surface, and thin box shapes for simple legs.

I'm picking caramel, chocolate, and cream tones for the snail shell, then writing the spiral-generation loop: computing a logarithmic radius growth, a tapering height, and a local position along the spiral, with cross-section offsets approximated using radial and up vectors to place stripe spheres around the tube, all transformed into world space via a matrix.

Now I'm adding scattered pebble spheres across the snail's body, using a seeded random generator to pick positions and sizes for roughly 70 small spheres along the foot.
